en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is an active stratovolcano renowned for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward into the Babuyan Channel.
Laguna de Bay, located southeast of Metro Manila, is the largest lake in the Philippines by surface area.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, peaking at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle is a large bird of prey endemic to the forests of Mindanao, Luzon, and Samar.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan is a karst landscape featuring an eight-kilometer underground river flowing into the sea.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected marine sanctuary featuring pristine coral atolls and diverse sea life.
The Verde Island Passage between Batangas and Mindoro holds the highest concentration of marine shorefish species in the world.
Baguio City sits in the Cordillera mountains at an elevation of 1,500 meters, giving it a cooler subtropical highland climate.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Sierra Madre mountain range stretches along the eastern coast of Luzon, acting as a natural barrier against Pacific typhoons.
The northernmost Batanes islands feature a unique subtropical climate and traditional Ivatan stone houses built to withstand strong typhoons.
